title: Senior Customer Success Manager
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2>The Company You’ll Join</h2> <p>Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. Built to replace fragmented tools with a single system of record, Carta brings together the software, services, and legal infrastructure that founders use to manage equity, fund managers use to run administration and reporting, and legal teams use to close transactions. Trusted by 55,000 companies and 1.8M+ equity holders in 160+ countries, and 10,000 funds and SPVs representing $250B+ in assets under management, Carta is transforming how private capital operates. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Fast Company, Inc. and Great Places to Work.</p> <p>For more information about our offices and culture, check out our <a href="https://carta.com/careers/">Carta careers page</a>.</p></div><h2>The Company You’ll Join </h2> <p>Carta is a platform that helps people manage equity, build businesses, and invest in the companies of tomorrow. Our mission is to unlock the power of equity ownership for more people in more places. </p> <p>Carta is trusted by more than 40,000 companies and over two million people in nearly 160 countries to manage cap tables, compensation, and valuations. Carta also supports nearly 7,000 funds and SPVs, and represents nearly $130B in assets under administration. title: Senior People Partner
description: Senior People Partner Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000 Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. THE MOMENT Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago. You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding. Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems. Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027): Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago. Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation. Background screening in Zinc. Security clearance coordination. Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting. Our working groups and committees. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that. Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join. Not yours Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition. The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO. Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO. THE STACK Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives. Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that. Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for. Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative. Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over. Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done. Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go. Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against. Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook. Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome. Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them. At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you. Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over. You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land. Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point. You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up. The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly. WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome. A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to. Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work. Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to. Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards. Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up. Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory. THE HONEST PART This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title. You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows. This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you. If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk. title: Strategic Client Manager
description: About Flock Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time. We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead. We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us! About the role Our largest fleet clients have the most vehicles, the most data and the most to gain from our connected proposition. As our Strategic Client Manager, you’ll be the main face of Flock for them, from multinationals and well-known brands to fast-growing sector leaders, and you’ll own those relationships end to end. Nearly all our business comes through brokers, so you’ll sit at the centre of the client, broker and Flock relationship, working closely with our Broker Development Managers and teams across the business. You’ll build our corporate client management approach from scratch, from account reviews and performance reporting to bringing claims, safety, underwriting and finance together for our biggest clients. You’ll report to our Head of Distribution and use AI day to day to prepare for meetings, understand accounts and improve reporting. Success means our clients stay with us and recommend us to others. What you’ll be doing Own the relationship with a portfolio of Flock’s largest fleet clients, becoming their primary point of contact and developing a strong understanding of their business. Build and run our corporate account management approach: client reviews, reporting, relationship cadence and account planning. Work closely with brokers and our Broker Development Managers to deliver a coordinated experience for every large corporate client. Bring together teams across Flock, including claims, safety, underwriting and finance, to resolve client questions and issues quickly, and build strong relationships with key stakeholders across client organisations. Identify retention risks early and create clear plans to protect our most important accounts. Help shape and improve Flock’s wider client service proposition, including account reviews, portal engagement, safety support, claims and reporting, feeding client feedback back into the business. Use AI in your day-to-day work, from account research and meeting preparation to query management, meeting summaries and client reporting. What you’ll need Strong experience within the insurance industry, with a clear understanding of the broker–client–insurer dynamic and the judgement to know where you add value, without duplicating the broker’s role, creating confusion or adding unnecessary layers for the client. Experience in a client-facing role such as insurer account or deal management, broker account management, claims relationship management or a similar position. A proven track record of managing important client relationships and delivering strong retention or customer satisfaction, with the confidence to work with senior stakeholders across clients, brokers and internal teams. Strong commercial judgement. You can identify when an account is at risk, understand what matters to the client and build a plan to retain them. Energy and ownership. You’re comfortable picking up a problem, finding the right people and driving it through to a solution. Confident using technology in your daily work, curious about how it can help you work faster and deliver a better client experience. Nice to have: experience with large, complex or multi-site corporate clients, Commercial Motor Fleet or fleet risk and safety experience, or exposure to claims or to building a client service proposition. Benefits 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖 Share Incentive Plan 📈 Workplace Pension 💰 Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options) Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵 Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣 £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓 £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻 We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. This role is expected to be field based rather than office based, so visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days. Making the world quantifiably safer takes more than good data. It takes a team where different perspectives are heard, and that’s a priority here. We insure fleets and drivers from every background, and we know a team built the same way makes sharper decisions and a better product for our customers. So we hire on merit, full stop, and we actively encourage applications from everyone. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway. Just come as your genuine self: the qualities and experiences only you bring are exactly what we want. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Assistant Financial Controller
description: About Flock Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time. We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead. We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us! About the role Reporting to our Financial Controller, you’ll own month-end for Flock’s finance team and strengthen the controls around it, running the close and producing the variance analysis and MI that FP&A and our senior team use for budgeting and reporting. We’re automating finance on our new platform and the team uses AI every day, so there’s plenty of room to improve how the work gets done as well as doing it. It suits a recently qualified accountant with strong core accounting from practice, who has already improved a process or control somewhere and wants to keep growing within the finance team. What you’ll be doing Own the month-end close from start to finish so it lands accurately and on time. Prepare balance sheet reconciliations and post journals, keeping the ledger clean and well evidenced. Run variance analysis and build the monthly MI pack, explaining what moved and why. Strengthen our financial controls and automate manual steps wherever you find them. Prepare our VAT returns and assist with group reporting. Work with FP&A so the numbers behind budgets and senior reporting are right. Support the annual audit and work alongside our external auditors. Use AI tools in your daily work to speed up reconciliations, analysis and reporting, and share what works with the team. Pick up ad hoc finance projects, including R&D tax claims if you have the experience. What you’ll need An ACA qualification, ideally recently qualified, although we’ll also consider strong ACCA or CIMA candidates. A practice background with hands-on month-end experience, whether from non-audit client work or time in industry. Big 4 or not makes no difference to us. Solid core accounting and close attention to detail, including balance sheet reconciliations, journals and variance analysis. Experience strengthening financial controls or improving a finance process, with an example you can talk us through. Curiosity and ambition, with the drive to push things forward and keep learning. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. Troubleshoot and resolve customers issues related to the Pleo product, and escalate to the appropriate internal team where needed. Provide feedback and support cross-functional teams on product development based on customer insights. Share learnings and contribute to our knowledge base to ensure growth and knowledge sharing across the team, and beyond. What you bring You’ll thrive in this role if you: Love providing fantastic, high-touch customer support on live chat, email and phone. Have a persistent and analytical approach to problem-solving. Fluency - Both written and spoken in Danish and English. title: Senior Operations Account Manager - Mandarin Speaking , London
description: Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone. THE TEAM • ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation The Opportunity Some of our biggest accounts are Chinese platforms, 3PLs and brokers moving millions of parcels into the UK. They grow with us when parcels arrive on time, issues get fixed fast, and someone on our side always knows exactly what’s going on. That someone is you. As our Mandarin-speaking Senior Operations Account Manager, you’ll take on some of the most complex of these accounts and set the standard for how we run account operations as we scale. Your mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure operations are never the reason a client hesitates to grow. Why This Role A team behind every client. We’ve rebuilt our growth engine around small pods of three, built to win together. A Growth Lead owns the commercial relationship, a Program Manager triages internally to get initiatives over the line, and you own the operation that makes every promise real. Same clients, same goals, same numbers. No one carries a client alone, and every win is shared. A real say in profitability. Margin is owned jointly by the pod through different lenses. When you cut parcel losses or make a collection run more efficiently, you’ll see exactly what it’s worth, and so will everyone else. Scale that keeps moving. We plan to more than double daily volume by July 2027 and open one or two international markets. Your accounts, and your role, grow with that. A career you can shape. Our Account Management team is tripling. Go deeper, taking on bigger and more complex accounts until you’re the expert the business leans on. Or go wider, across more pods, and in time lead others doing what you do. What You’ll Do Be the client’s go-to. Run the day-to-day relationship in Mandarin and English, on every channel, WeChat included. Own performance end to end. Know every metric that matters to your clients inside out, from on-time delivery to lost and undelivered parcels, and what’s driving each one. Then own every escalation from first report to final fix. Set the weekly rhythm. Lead weekly business reviews so clients hear the news from you first, good or bad. Make the forecast real. You won’t take a client’s forecast at face value. You’ll challenge it, sharpen it, and become the person whose numbers the network plans around. Protect the margin. Spot when an account’s profitability starts to slip, find the leak, and bring the recovery plan before anyone asks. Fix things once. Turn recurring issues into permanent fixes with our operations, quality and finance teams, then share them across every pod. Who Will Thrive in This Role? You’re the person others call when a problem gets complicated, and you like it that way. You’ve led operational improvements that went beyond a single account, and you can show what they were worth. You can run a fix across operations, quality and finance at once: you map the dependencies, manage the risk and bring people with you. You’d rather deliver bad news early than let a client find it first, and you never quote a number you can’t back up. You spot a slipping account before it turns red, and you have the plan ready before anyone asks. You’d rather fix something once for everyone than twice for yourself, and you share the credit. You love making other people better: you coach, spot strengths and help others use them. You switch between Mandarin with clients and English with internal teams without losing nuance. Must-Haves 6+ years in an operational, account management or client-facing role in logistics, supply chain, cross-border e-commerce or a related field. A track record of running high-volume, complex client operations and leading cross-team improvements to measurable results. Fluent Mandarin Chinese and English, written and spoken. Comfort with data: you can challenge a forecast, read a performance dashboard and size an operational issue. Sound operational judgement when things don’t go to plan, and a bias for action. A clear, structured communication style, from a quick update to a formal escalation. Compensation & Benefits Generous equity, richer than 99% of European startups, with annual top-ups to share Relay’s success. Private health & dental coverage, so comprehensive you’d need to be a partner at a Magic Circle law firm to match it. 25 days of holidays. Enhanced parental leave. Located in Shoreditch, our office set-up enables the kind of in-person interactions that drive impact. We work 4 days on-site, with 1 day remote. Hardware of your choice. Extensive perks (gym subsidies, cycle-to-work, Friday office lunch, covered Uber home and dinner for late nights, and more). Fast and Focused Hiring Process Talent Acquisition Interview (45 min) Hiring Manager Interview (60 min) Case Study (90 min) Culture & Team Fit Conversation (30 min) Decision and offer within 48 hours; our process mirrors our pace of work. Who Thrives at Relay? Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously. Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction. 1% Better Every Day : You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience. All In, All the Time : You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts. People-Powered Greatness : You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success. Grow the Whole Pie : You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we. If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect. engineering and product teams.</li> <li><strong>Hands-On Project Delivery:</strong> Run individual projects directly when a programme needs it.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Prioritisation & Product Partnership</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Executive Prioritisation:</strong> Bring options, costs and trade-offs to executives and secure a clear decision on what comes first.</li> <li><strong>Backlog Management:</strong> Manage the backlog for your programmes so engineering teams always know what is next and why.</li> <li><strong>Product Collaboration:</strong> Work with product managers to turn business goals into well-defined, deliverable pieces of work.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Reporting, Risk & Vendors</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Honest Reporting:</strong> Give executives and stakeholders clear, candid updates on progress, risks and dates.</li> <li><strong>Risk & Dependency Management:</strong> Find risks, blockers and cross-team dependencies early, resolve them, and escalate when a decision is needed.</li> <li><strong>Vendor Management:</strong> Hold external vendors and delivery partners to their commitments and fit their work into our plans and releases.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Continuous Improvement</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Ways of Working:</strong> Improve how we plan, track and report on delivery across the technology organisation.</li> </ul> <p><strong>A day in the life</strong></p> <p>Your day is split between the teams doing the work and the leaders deciding what the work should be. You might start with an engineering team, checking progress against the plan and clearing a blocker, then spend time with a product manager breaking a loyalty feature into deliverable stages. In the afternoon you could review a vendor’s delivery plan for a marketing technology integration, then update programme status ahead of an executive review, where you’ll set out where things stand, what is at risk and which decisions you need. You’ll leave with clear priorities and take them back to the teams.</p> <p><strong>What skills and experience do I need for this role?</strong></p> <p><strong>Essential Requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Highly Skilled in technical programme or project management.</li> <li>Experience working directly with software engineering teams.</li> <li>Adept at delivering customer-facing websites or mobile apps.</li> <li>Excellent at managing programmes across several teams, including planning, dependency management and release coordination.</li> <li>Experience running prioritisation and backlog management with senior stakeholders and reporting on delivery to executives.</li> <li>Managing both external vendors or delivery partners.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Desirable Attributes</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with websites and ecommerce at large scale: high traffic, many markets, or several brands.</li> <li>Experience delivering programmes in personalisation, loyalty or digital marketing technology.</li> <li>Experience delivering native mobile apps alongside web.</li> <li>Experience in retail, particularly nutrition or beauty.</li> <li>A record of bringing clear structure to ambiguous, multi-team programmes.</li> <li>Strong written communication, with the ability to explain a complex programme to executives in plain terms.</li> </ul> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>THG is proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. title: Head of Legal
description: Head of Legal 📍Manchester | 💰 £120,000 - £150,000 Street Group is a fast moving B2B SaaS business - grown in Manchester but on a UK wide mission to make moving house as easy as buying a car. We’ve recently raised strategic growth investment, and are scaling fast toward an ambitious growth plan. To support this growth, we're moving from fractional legal support to our first full-time in-house lawyer. As we grow and our product and client base expand, we need someone who can own the legal function day to day. As this is our first full-time legal hire, we're looking for a self-starter who is passionate about the role and who will build, own and manage our internal legal function, creating value and protecting the business from risk. You’ll work autonomously and efficiently, leading on legal matters and bringing in external counsel where required, and you’ll report directly to our CFO. How you'll make a difference Take ownership of the legal function, including a smooth handover from the current fractional counsel. Lead on B2B SaaS contracting: draft, negotiate and manage customer, partner and supplier agreements, and maintain contract templates and playbooks. Update terms and conditions as new product features are released, working closely with product, sales and commercial colleagues. Act as product counsel on AI-enabled features: advise product and engineering on the legal and regulatory implications of AI in Street Group’s products (including data use and training, IP and output ownership, accuracy and liability, and transparency), and ensure customer terms, data terms and product documentation reflect them. Advise on data protection, privacy and information security, including customer-facing data terms and requirements. Work with compliance and governance colleagues to establish and maintain corporate governance, AI governance and policy, and compliance frameworks. Identify and adopt AI tools and legal technology within the function to improve speed, consistency and capacity. Manage relationships with external law firms, including specialist advisers retained for equity and other matters, to ensure cost-effective use of external spend. Support M&A and other strategic transactions, including legal due diligence and post-acquisition integration. Identify and manage legal risks ahead of any future diligence or exit process. Advise the executive team and, as required, the Board on legal, regulatory and risk matters. Keep up to date with legislative and regulatory change affecting the business. Who we're looking for You’re qualified to practise in England and Wales, with 8+ years’ PQE gained in a law firm, in-house, or both. You have strong experience drafting and negotiating B2B SaaS agreements, ideally with institutional or regulated customers. You’re commercially focused: you act as a partner to sales, product and senior leadership and balance legal risk with commercial objectives. You have a sound understanding of data protection law and practical exposure to information security and technology risk. You have up-to-date knowledge of AI regulation and market practice as it affects SaaS products, with experience of advising on, or contracting around, AI features and of how customers and regulators are approaching them. You take a forward-thinking approach to AI and legal technology, with a track record of applying it to legal work. You’ve built or scaled a legal function, including templates, processes and external counsel management. You’re able to work autonomously as the sole in-house lawyer, with the judgement to know when to escalate or bring in specialists. You have excellent negotiation, communication and problem-solving skills, and you turn complex legal issues into practical, business-oriented advice. You manage multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment. Bonus points if… You’ve worked in an FCA-regulated business. You’ve worked in a private equity-backed business. You have M&A experience, including due diligence and post-deal integration. You’ve had exposure to governance, company secretarial and ESG matters. Why Join Us? A role with genuine commercial impact - you won’t be a support function here Direct access to the Co-Founders and leadership team Hybrid working from our Manchester office, with the option to WFH 3 days a week. Guilt-Free R&R - £1000 towards a holiday after your first year with the team (we'll even cover the tax!) Joining a culture that supports your development and encourages growth £500 yearly L&D budget for your career development Your birthday on us - we pay, you stay away ‘Give something back’ - 2 paid days volunteering on us Enhanced maternity, paternity & adoption pay Mental health & well-being support via Health Assured Regular well-being initiatives Flexible working hours Public transport season ticket loans Paid menopause leave Holiday buying scheme Be a part of something bigger - everyone in our team is passionate about improving the entire property industry! It's a huge goal, but it motivates us to do better every single day A chance to work on cutting-edge technology Comfortable, relaxed office space - office dogs welcome! Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and were about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria; please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application! Salary £120k - £150k dependent on experience. However, sometimes the perfect person is far more or less experienced than we anticipated. In these situations, planned ranges go out the window. If you think that might be the case, please apply and just let us know. We care deeply about helping the tech industry become a more inclusive and diverse place and we work hard to lead by example. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a complementary team of employees and building an inclusive environment for all. Candidates must be eligible to live and work in the UK and be able to perform the work specified. Interview Process 3 stages = Video call with our Head of People > Technical Interview > Values interview. We want to make our interviews as inclusive as possible, so if you need any adjustments made, or if there's anything you think we should be aware of during the interview process, please do let us know. A note on using AI in your job application As a fast-moving and rapidly evolving tech company, we embrace the advantages of AI and encourage its use throughout our application process. However, our goal is to get to know and hire the authentic you - your skills, experience, and values. We don’t want to hire an AI-generated version of you. We consider AI to be a valuable tool, not something that should overshadow you as an individual. How we use AI in the hiring process Candidate experience is really important to us, and our Talent team use AI notetakers during interviews so they can focus purely on their conversation with you. All hiring decisions are made by humans - not AI. Let us know if you have any questions! Compensation: £120K – £150K • £120K – £150K Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Security Operations Analyst
description: About Lendable Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start: One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK Profitable since 2017 Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot ) So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance . We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days. We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes. Join us if you want to Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1 Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions Build the best technology in-house : we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting About the Role Lendable is a high-growth FinTech building its security operations capability deliberately. As a Senior Security Operations Analyst, you will triage and respond to security alerts, help improve the quality of the detections behind them, and lead the response when a security event becomes an incident. You will investigate alerts and escalations from our MSSP, tune our monitoring so that it finds more of what matters and less of what doesn’t, and act as a trusted Incident Commander for security incidents, from declaration through to post-incident review. You will work with Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders, and you will be credible with all of them. AI is used widely across the business, in how we build software, run operations and serve customers, and that changes both what security incidents look like and how quickly we can respond to them. You will use AI and automation as a normal part of your work, and you will be able to investigate and respond to incidents where AI tooling is the cause, the target or the route in. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone with hands-on SOC experience and a track record of commanding incidents. What You’ll Be Doing 1. Alert Triage & Monitoring Triage and investigate alerts across our SIEM, EDR, identity and cloud tooling, taking escalations from our MSSP’s first-line team. Reduce false positives and alert fatigue by tuning detection rules, thresholds and suppressions. Utilise AI and automation to speed up triage, enrichment and response, and to remove repetitive manual work from the analyst workflow. 2. Incident Command & Response Command security incidents, coordinating technical response, decision-making and communications across Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders. Give clear, timely updates to executives during live incidents. Lead or support technical investigation and containment across endpoint, identity and cloud (AWS/GCP) environments, including incidents involving AI use, such as prompt injection, or credentials exposed through AI-generated code. Run blameless post-incident reviews, track actions to closure, and feed lessons back into detection, playbooks and controls. Take part in the out-of-hours on-call rota. 3. Operational Reporting & Assurance Track and report SecOps metrics that reflect reality, such as alert quality, time to triage, time to contain, incident volumes and root causes. Maintain accurate incident records and evidence in our incident management platform to support audit and assurance activity. Build working relationships with Engineering, Platform and IT Systems so that incident response is practised before it is needed. What We’re Looking For Proven incident command: Demonstrable experience leading significant security incidents as Incident Commander or lead responder, from declaration to resolution and review. You can describe incidents you have run, the decisions you made and what you changed afterwards. Technical investigation skills: Solid hands-on SOC/DFIR experience, including log analysis, endpoint and identity investigation, and cloud incident response in AWS or GCP. AI fluency: You understand how AI use creates security risk, including data exposure, agent misuse and AI-assisted attacks, and you can investigate and contain incidents that involve it. AI-first ways of working: You already use AI and automation to speed up your own work, whether in investigation, enrichment, detection engineering or reporting, and you can judge when to trust the output and when to check it. Composure and influence: You stay calm and structured under pressure, and can direct engineers and senior stakeholders without formal authority over them. Communication: You can brief a senior leader in plain language during a live incident, and write a post-incident report that an engineer, an auditor and a board member can each use. Pragmatism: You understand that security supports a business moving quickly, and you balance risk, speed and proportionality in your decisions. Regulated environment awareness (desirable): Experience in financial services or another regulated sector, including incident reporting and evidence expectations. Certifications (desirable, not required): GCIH, GCFA, GCIA, or equivalent practical experience. Interview process A quick phone call with one of the talent team A Hiring Manager call with our Head of InfoSec Technical Interview with two of the team Final stage interview with our VP of Engineering Life at Lendable Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner. Check out our blog ! Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Dex - Staff Product Engineer
description: Our Mission Human time and effort is the rarest thing in the universe. The fact that so many people hate what they do for work is a disaster on so many levels. How many people live quiet lives of misery? How many generational talents do we miss due to circumstance? Dex’s mission is to close the gap between Talent & Opportunity, we believe that work, and being productive, is part of the human condition, that regardless of AI, human passion, ingenuity and a desire to do things means that work will always exist. We are building Dex to create a future where technology helps every individual to understand their strengths, interests and unique abilities, and to connect with opportunities where they can thrive, because more people doing things they love leads to a better, happier and more productive world. We are starting by connecting the world's most ambitious software engineers with the companies that deserve them. The Role This is a Staff-level full-stack product role with a backend-heavy centre of gravity. You'll own complete product slices end-to-end — things like a candidate database with rich search and filtering, a dashboard that surfaces call transcripts and match history for our Talent Operations team, and the workflows that let them stack-rank candidates against a new role in minutes rather than hours. You ship these without needing to be guided step by step. You're not a specialist who hands off at the API boundary. You think in user outcomes and delivery units, and you're reliable: your code handles edge cases, your APIs have clean contracts, and the work you ship stays shipped. What You'll Do Own product delivery — take features from spec to production, backend-first but covering frontend and integration where needed Build and maintain backend systems — product APIs, data pipelines, and core infrastructure on our Python/FastAPI/Postgres stack Build with LLMs and agents — ship product features with significant LLM integration; description: Why Faculty? We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here . We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence. Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology. AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen. About Frontier Faculty Frontier™ is a decision operating system. It puts AI to work on the decisions that matter most to large organisations, such as where to invest, how to allocate resources, and when to act. Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business. Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city. We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system. Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Over months they connect it into a wider decision network, and over years they build an adaptive enterprise. Frontier is built by Faculty, an AI company that has delivered more than 400 systems since 2014 and is now part of Accenture. About Design at Frontier We’re a small team, growing deliberately - we’d rather have five designers who trust each other than fifteen who don't. We're tightly integrated with engineering. We prototype in code. We co-own the design system with developers. We're actively exploring what agentic-augmented design work looks like in practice, not in think pieces — and we're honest when we don't have the answer yet. We’re active in shaping the product culture at Frontier; putting people first, raising the quality bar and ensuring a coherent experience. You’ll be part of shaping that culture. About the role You'll be one of the most senior designers on Frontier, shaping a product that's still early enough that the decisions you make will define how it works for years. Day to day, you'll be designing the surfaces where people and agents collaborate on real clinical decisions — how evidence gets surfaced, how recommendations get explained, how humans push back, how teams learn. This is hard, unsolved design work. The existing patterns for AI interfaces mostly come from consumer chat products; they don't transfer cleanly to environments where the cost of a bad decision is measured in years of research or patient outcomes. You'll be expected to work end-to-end: from framing the problem with product and engineering, through prototyping in code and design canvases, through shipping. You'll help set the craft bar for the team, mentor the designers around you, and push back when something isn't good enough yet. What you'll work on Designing the core interaction patterns for how humans and agents collaborate inside a decision loop. description: About Numan Founded in 2018, we’ve already grown to be a 300+ team distributed across the globe, united by a singular mission: empowering people to take control of their health. Numan is transforming health: we’ve built a cutting-edge platform that integrates diagnostics, medication, supplements, digital programmes, and doctor consultations. Giving people the tools they need to maximise life. To deliver on our transformative mission, we are guided by our 5 company values: • Patients first. • Learn fast. • Own the quality. • Succeed together. • Care deeply. Backed by top-tier investors, Numan is already having a positive impact on hundreds of thousands of patients here in the UK, and we want you to help us deliver this mission! The Role: This is a new role at Numan. It marks a significant intent in how we want to operate and invest in areas that make a meaningful impact to business performance. This role will report directly to our Founder & CEO and serve as a trusted advisor and partner to our Board, Executive team, and cross-functional leaders across Product, Commercial, and Growth Marketing. As an established D2C Growth leader, you will be a big influencer on our growth culture more broadly. You'll be: Leading the company’s growth mission, acting as a trusted board advisor to investors and board members, clearly articulating Numan’s growth strategy, cohort dynamics, strategic bets, and capital allocation. Coaching and developing growth marketing leadership teams while raising execution pace, energy, and commercial ambition across the entire business. Formulating growth hypotheses and balancing macro market shifts with unit economics like CAC, LTV, and payback periods to validate and de-risk high-stakes investments. Rapidly diagnosing growth bottlenecks and building high-velocity multi-channel engines, focused on compounding growth. Serving as a culture beacon across the organisation to inspire and align teams that directly or indirectly impact revenue opportunities and growth levers. Monitoring full-funnel performance metrics daily to extract maximum leverage from lean budgets, scaling winning channels rapidly and pivoting decisively before returns diminish. Pioneering data and AI-driven growth across creative production, rapid experimentation, and advanced measurement. You'll have: Significant experience in building consumer businesses, either as a founder, operator holding roles directly responsible for growth. Proven track record scaling consumer businesses through major revenue step-changes (£10–100m, or £100m–250m+) navigating high-growth environments. Significant exposure to building toward substantial enterprise value creation in a growth or GTM role. Hands-on experience building new channels from scratch and navigating real operational battles, strategic pivots, and market headwinds. Experience shaping company growth strategy at the board level alongside founders and executive teams. A formidable combination of deep data analytics, performance marketing, and cutting-edge tools, balancing a strategic macro view with an extreme focus on execution. You have a strong bias for action and not just theory. Total comfort navigating ambiguity and shifting markets, with a practical, analytical approach to making decisions and managing lean resources. Our benefits include... 📈 - Share options. 🏖 - 25 days holiday, plus bank holidays (increasing to 30 the longer you stay with Numan). 🩺 - Health insurance with Vitality . 🚘 - Electric car salary sacrifice scheme with Octopus . 🧸 - Enhanced maternity and parental leave. 🥳 - A day off on your Birthday! 🐥 - Nursery benefit provided by YellowNest . 💼 - Employee assistance programme (access to therapy, financial planning and discounts). ⚖️ - Generous pension (includes both employee and employer contributions). 💻 - Flexible working options, including a dog-friendly office in Farringdon. 📚 - Personal training and development budget via Learnerbly. 👟 - Wellhub membership, giving you access to over 2,000 locations in the UK. 🚲 - Cycle to work scheme. 🚆 - Season ticket loan. % - Discount on Numan products for your friends and family. 🤲 - Paid volunteering days. 📅 - An additional 2 weeks off once you reach your 5th anniversary with Numan. Diversity at Numan At Numan, people are at the heart of who we are. We recognise and value the unique perspectives and experiences that individuals from all backgrounds bring. We promote innovation and creativity, enabling us to tackle things from various viewpoints and are committed to equal opportunities and continuously strive to create a workplace where everyone feels respected, heard, and valued. Embracing diversity isn't just our goal; it's our strength, driving us towards a more inclusive future. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Product Designer
description: <div class="content-intro"><div> <div> <div class="gmail_quote"> <div> <div><span id="m_-113912706363268805m_-2746164444908759431gmail-docs-internal-guid-131e4fb0-7fff-b4e9-ff50-e8cf32449b1b">CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at <a href="https://www.coreweave.com">www.coreweave.com</a>.</span></div> <div> </div> <div>We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.</div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <p> </p></div><p><strong>About Physical AI</strong></p> <p>CoreWeave's Physical AI team helps companies apply AI to the physical systems they design, test, and operate, across automotive, industrial, robotics, and autonomous vehicles (AV).</p> <p>We work as one cross-functional team of product, design, engineering, and forward-deployed engineers, partnering directly with our customers' engineering teams.</p> <p>Our focus is twofold: making AI usable for engineers who know their machines in depth but are not ML specialists, and supporting robotics and AV teams across the full development loop, from sensor data and simulation to model training and evaluation.</p> <h3><strong>What You’ll Do:</strong></h3> <p>As a <strong>Staff Product Designer</strong> on the Physical AI team, you will lead design across our portfolio of Physical AI products, turning complex data and ML workflows into tools that engineers who build vehicles, machines, and robots trust and use every day. You'll bring strong design craft and sharp product judgment to a new product area, setting direction and framing ambiguous problems.</p> <p>This is a role with real breadth. You'll own the end-to-end experience across a number of products, from the customer-facing apps engineers use day to day to the builder tools our Field team use to create and publish those apps. You'll set a shared design vision for the portfolio and consolidate our Physical AI products into the broader CoreWeave design language, so they reuse proven patterns and feel like part of one platform. You'll also spend time with customer engineering teams to understand their workflows, data, and constraints, turning what you learn into clear problem framing for Product and Engineering.</p> <p>We're looking for a designer who uses AI tools as a core part of their workflow today, to prototype, test ideas, and explore more options in less time. Comfort with technical complexity and a bias toward experimentation are essential here.</p> <p>As the most senior designer on the Physical AI team, you'll mentor the designers you work alongside, raise the craft bar, and shape how design works with Product, Engineering, and Field Engineering. You'll be joining a small, high-trust design team. The work is broad, the impact is real, and there's room to shape how design operates at one of the fastest-growing infrastructure companies in the world.</p> <p><strong>Who You Are:</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years of experience as a versatile designer who can own all facets of design, including user research, UX, interaction design, prototyping, and UI design.</li> <li>An excellent portfolio showcasing user-centered problem solving through interaction design, visual design, and systems thinking.</li> <li>Deep proficiency with Figma and a solid understanding of building usable, accessible, and modular designs that scale.</li> <li>Experience partnering with Product and Engineering to define strategy and solve complex problems for technical users in B2B, infrastructure, developer tools, or platform contexts.</li> <li>Actively incorporates AI tools into your design workflow, using them to move faster, prototype smarter, and tackle harder problems.</li> <li>Comfortable working with technical complexity and ambiguity; you help teams frame problems, not just resolve them.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with front-end technologies such as HTML, CSS, or modern frameworks for prototyping or implementation.</li> <li>Familiarity with ML concepts such as training, evaluation, and deployment, or with simulation and test workflows.</li> <li>Familiarity with cloud infrastructure or enterprise platform products.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Wondering if you’re a good fit? We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams – even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk. </strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Care deeply about users:</strong> You love connecting with real users daily, helping them solve issues and understand good patterns for using our tools. You approach questions and requests with a kind, thoughtful tone that makes users feel appreciated and connected to our team.</li> <li><strong>Autonomous:</strong> You work well in a self-directed environment, proactively finding ways to improve processes and collaborate with team members or engaged users.</li> <li><strong>Curious and driven:</strong> You are eager to explore machine learning and learn more about the engineering stack and common ML workflows, solving problems in both fast-paced, short-term sprints and in larger, long-term projects.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Why Us?</strong></h3> <p>We work hard, have fun, and move fast! We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Be Curious at Your Core</strong></li> <li><strong>Act Like an Owner</strong></li> <li><strong>Empower Employees</strong></li> <li><strong>Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences</strong></li> <li><strong>Achieve More Together</strong></li> </ul> <p>We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for takeoff, the growth opportunities within the organization are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>To fulfill our obligation to protect client data, successful applicants offered employment with CoreWeave will be required to complete a basic criminal record check, conducted in compliance with GDPR. Employment offers are conditional upon receiving satisfactory check results.</em></p> <p><strong>What We Offer</strong></p> <p>In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs, including:</p> <ul> <li>Family-level Medical Insurance</li> <li>Family-level Dental Insurance </li> <li>Generous Pension Contribution </li> <li>Life Assurance at 4x Salary </li> <li>Critical Illness Cover </li> <li>Employee Assistance Programme </li> <li>Tuition Reimbursement</li> <li>Work culture focused on innovative disruption</li> </ul> <p><em>Benefits may vary by location. </em></p> <p><strong>Equal Opportunity </strong></p> <p><em>CoreWeave is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace. All qualified applicants and candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information.</em></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><strong>Recruitment Agencies</strong></span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;"><em><em data-stringify-type="italic">CoreWeave does not accept speculative CVs. Any unsolicited CVs received will be treated as the property of CoreWeave and your Terms & Conditions associated with the use of CVs will be considered null and void.</em></em></span></p> <p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;"><em data-stringify-type="italic">Any unsolicited CVs sent by your company to us – that is to say, in any situation where we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy – will be considered by us to be a “free gift”, leaving us liable for no fees whatsoever should we choose to contact the candidate directly and engage the candidate’s services, and will in no way establish any prior claim by your company to representation of that candidate should the candidate’s details also be submitted by any other party.</em></span></em></p> <p><strong>Export Control Compliance</strong></p> <p><em>This position requires access to technology and/or source code subject to U.S. export control laws. Any such access will be provided only in compliance with applicable U.S. export control requirements. As part of the recruitment process, CoreWeave may request limited information reasonably necessary to assess applicable export-control requirements. </em></p> <p><strong>Updated privacy notice - UK and EU Job Applications </strong></p> <p><em>When you apply to a job on this site, the personal data contained in your application will be collected by CoreWeave UK Ltd. (“Controller”), which is located at</em></p> <p><em>Phosphor (6th Floor), 133 Park Street, London, SE1 9EA</em></p> <p><em>and can be contacted by emailing ----- Controller’s data protection officer can be contacted at ----- Your personal data will be processed for the purposes of managing Controller’s recruitment related activities, which include setting up and conducting interviews and tests for applicants, evaluating and assessing the results thereto, and as is otherwise needed in the recruitment and hiring processes. Such processing is legally permissible under Art. 6(1)(f) of (i) Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation (“GDPR”) and (ii) the GDPR as it forms part of the laws of the UK (“UK GDPR”), as necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the Controller, which are the solicitation, evaluation, and selection of applicants for employment. Your personal data will be shared with Greenhouse Software, Inc., a cloud services provider located in the United States of America and engaged by Controll

description: <div class="content-intro"><div> <div> <div class="gmail_quote"> <div> <div><span id="m_-113912706363268805m_-2746164444908759431gmail-docs-internal-guid-131e4fb0-7fff-b4e9-ff50-e8cf32449b1b">CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Learn more at <a href="https://www.coreweave.com">www.coreweave.com</a>.</span></div> <div> </div> <div>We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.</div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <p> </p></div><h3><strong>What You'll Do:</strong></h3> <p>CoreWeave’s Physical AI Engineering team builds and scales the core platform powering advanced engineering simulation and AI workflows. Our ambition is to become the super-intelligent AI test lab for the engineering industry, delivering the performant, reliable, and scalable foundation trusted by the world’s largest engineering companies.</p> <p><strong>About the role: </strong></p> <p>The Staff Frontend Engineer will own and evolve the Physical AI platform’s product surface: the data-heavy, workflow-centric web experience where engineers design experiments, compare runs, interact with agents, and convert complex test data into decisions. Operating at Staff-level scope (with openness to exceptional Senior Frontend Engineers ready to step into staff-level impact), you will own the frontend end-to-end-including component architecture, design system evolution, performance optimization, and production operations. In this role, you will collaborate closely with Design, Product, and Backend Engineering to design intuitive UIs for complex workflows, shape Python-backed API contracts, and integrate agentic capabilities safely. Additionally, you will drive frontend developer experience improvements, maintain high testing standards, and mentor engineers across the wider organisation.</p> <h3><strong>Who You Are:</strong></h3> <ul> <li>7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a track record of building, maintaining, and architecting complex, data-heavy web applications at Senior or Staff scope.</li> <li>Advanced proficiency in React, TypeScript, and web fundamentals, with deep experience structuring large-scale frontends across modules, state management, routing, and data-fetching patterns.</li> <li>Proven background building visualization-centric UIs, dashboards, charts, time-series metrics, or experiment explorers for complex datasets.</li> <li>Hands-on experience integrating frontends with We operate at the intersection of advanced cloud infrastructure and applied data science, transforming how complex industrial products - such as automotive systems, aircraft, and advanced batteries - are conceived, tested, and developed.</p> <p><strong>About the role:</strong></p> <p>As a Senior Applied Researcher, you will take end-to-end ownership of complex machine learning problems across the Physical AI space. This is a high-impact role for someone with a strong technical foundation and a generalist mindset who can move from problem framing and experimentation through deployment and ongoing support.</p> <p>You will work closely with engineering, product, and client-facing teams to turn advanced ML methods into production-ready solutions that can be trusted in real customer environments. The role blends research depth with practical delivery, and requires someone who can align stakeholders, surface risks and limitations, and communicate technical decisions clearly.</p> <p><strong>Who You Are:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, or applied AI, with evidence of delivering high-impact production ML systems.</li> <li>Strong software engineering skills in Python, with extensive experience using scientific computing and ML libraries such as NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.</li> <li>Experience deploying and supporting ML systems in production, including cloud-based environments.</li> <li>Strong grounding in statistical modelling, machine learning experimentation, and evaluation.</li> <li>Experience working with time-series, high-dimensional, or imperfect real-world datasets.</li> <li>Strong technical curiosity and a habit of keeping up with current ML and AI research.</li> <li>Comfortable working cross-functionally with engineering, product, and customer-facing teams, and able to explain technical decisions clearly to different audiences.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred: (if applicable)</strong></p> <ul> <li>Background in engineering, physics, chemistry, or another STEM discipline connected to complex physical systems.</li> <li>Experience with anomaly detection, optimisation, reliability-focused modelling, or related approaches in industrial settings.</li> <li>Experience building or experimenting with agents or autonomous systems.</li> <li>Familiarity with MLOps, model monitoring, and efficient compute practices.</li> <li>Experience working with sparse, noisy, or imperfect real-world data from labs, heavy industry, or other applied environments.</li> <li>Track record of collaborating closely with deployed or client-facing teams to bring advanced methods into operational use.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Wondering if you’re a good fit? </strong><strong>We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams – even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match.</strong><strong> Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk. </strong></p> <ul> <li>You love applying advanced ML to real-world, high-value physical engineering problems.</li> <li>You're curious about agentic and autonomous approaches and how they can reshape engineering workflows.</li> <li>You're an expert in taking ML solutions from research and modelling through production delivery, with a strong bias toward reusable, high-quality systems.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Why CoreWeave?</strong></p> <p>At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast!  We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. description: <div class="content-intro"><h3 id="isPasted"><strong>Company Overview</strong></h3> <p>Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.</p> <p>Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.</p> <p>At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game.
